overview: Six-month QI project using the Model for Improvement: two mapping sessions in December 2026, then PDSA cycles from January to June 2027, with every thrombolysis case plotted on a run chart against the 2025 to 2026 baseline.
population: All patients thrombolysed for acute ischaemic stroke at the hospital from January to June 2027 (about 45 to 50 cases), day and night.
exposure: Changes tested in sequence: cycle 1 direct-to-CT on the ambulance stretcher for pre-alerted patients in weekday daytime; cycle 2 a single group page on pre-alert; cycle 3 drug preparation during CT; cycle 4 extension of cycles 1 to 3 to nights and weekends; nurse-led two-minute debriefs after every case throughout.
procedures: The stroke nurse adds arrival-to-CT and CT-to-decision times to the timing sheet. Mapping sessions include paramedics, emergency nurses, a CT radiographer, the stroke team and pharmacy, and follow a no-blame rule: steps are discussed, not people. The run chart is reviewed at a monthly meeting with every treated mimic and haemorrhage.

outcomes.name: Door-to-needle time
outcomes.measure: Minutes from hospital arrival to thrombolytic bolus, per case
outcomes.why: The measure the aim targets and the network reports.

outcomes.name: Treated within 45 minutes
outcomes.measure: Proportion of cases per two-month block

outcomes.name: Arrival-to-CT and CT-to-decision times
outcomes.measure: Minutes per case from the extended timing sheet
outcomes.why: Shows which change moved which step.

outcomes.name: Symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage
outcomes.measure: Numerator and denominator per two-month block
outcomes.why: Speed must not come at the cost of safety.

outcomes.name: Treated stroke mimics
outcomes.measure: Numerator and denominator; each case reviewed
outcomes.why: Faster pathways can treat more mimics.

outcomes.name: Trauma CT delayed by a stroke case
outcomes.measure: Count of trauma scans started late because a stroke patient was on the table

feasibility: Uses existing staff, the existing timing sheet with two added fields and a monthly meeting; about 45 to 50 cases in six months.
biasMitigation: Out-of-hours cases marked on the chart

biasFlags.label: Secular trend in the network
biasFlags.note: Network-wide campaigns are annotated on the chart.

biasFlags.label: Incomplete step timings
biasFlags.note: The stroke nurse checks each sheet within 24 hours.

flags: Three balancing measures because each change carries a different risk
parsimony.simplestPath: One run chart of every case with the baseline median.

theoreticalFramework: Model for Improvement with PDSA cycles; SEIPS to describe work-system factors found in mapping.
summary: Four PDSA cycles over six months with case-level run charts and three balancing measures.
